method: Step 1 — Name the standard and paragraph

Cite the Ind AS and paragraph ICAI uses (e.g. 'para 32 of Ind AS 103', 'para B96 of Ind AS 110', 'para 28 of Ind AS 28'). In a case scenario first say what kind of investee it is: subsidiary, joint operation, joint venture, associate or financial asset.
Step 2 — Work the numbers in ICAI's layout

Goodwill table (consideration + NCI + previously held interest − net assets at fair value); NCI working; pre- and post-acquisition split of reserves; elimination of intra-group items and unrealised profit; journal entries for ownership changes and loss of control.
Step 3 — Conclude with the treatment and amounts
State where each amount goes: goodwill, capital reserve (OCI/equity), profit or loss, other equity, NCI. For consolidated balance sheets follow Division II of Schedule III.
Show the goodwill working even if the final figure is wrong. Never take a bargain purchase to profit or loss under Ind AS. Changes in stake without losing control never touch goodwill or P&L.
changes: Study material applicable from May 2026 onwards is the Nov 2024 edition (Aug 2025 reprint). Ind AS 28 carve-out: uniform policies for associates 'unless impracticable'.

formulas.title: Consolidation building blocks
formulas.idea: Add everything line by line, take out what is inside the group, and split equity between the parent and outsiders.

master.name: Consolidated equity split
master.expr: Group reserves = Parent's reserves + Parent % × Post-acquisition reserves of subsidiary − Parent's share of unrealised profit; NCI = NCI at acquisition + NCI % × Post-acquisition reserves − NCI's share of upstream unrealised profit
master.logic: The parent owns its own savings plus its slice of what the subsidiary has saved since joining the family.
master.cue: prepare consolidated balance sheet; pre- and post-acquisition profits

items.name: Goodwill at acquisition
items.expr: Goodwill = Consideration + NCI + FV of previously held interest − Net identifiable assets at FV
items.derive: Computed once, at the date control is obtained.
items.cue: acquired x% of a company; fair value of net assets
items.trap: Recomputing goodwill when the stake later changes without loss of control.

items.name: Unrealised profit in closing inventory
items.expr: URP = Intra-group stock held × Profit margin on the transfer (eliminated 100%); NCI bears its % only if upstream
items.logic: The group cannot earn profit by selling to itself; take it out until sold outside.
items.derive: Deducted in the master formula; who bears it depends on the seller.
items.hook: Upstream → share with NCI; downstream → parent alone.
items.cue: goods sold by subsidiary to parent (or vice versa) remaining in stock at a mark-up
items.trap: Eliminating only the parent's percentage of the profit.

items.name: Effective interest in a sub-subsidiary
items.expr: Group % = Π holdings down the chain + direct holding; NCI % = 100% − Group %
items.logic: 80% of 60% is 48% — the rest of S2 belongs to outsiders, directly or through S1.
items.derive: Group % feeds the master formula for the sub-subsidiary.
items.cue: P holds S1 which holds S2
items.trap: Treating S2 as not a subsidiary because the group holds under 50%.

items.name: Parent's share with cumulative preference shares held by NCI
items.expr: Parent's share = (Profit − Preference dividend whether declared or not) × Parent %
items.logic: Preference holders get their fixed slice first.
items.derive: Adjusts post-acquisition profit in the master formula.
items.cue: cumulative preference shares of subsidiary held by outsiders

formulas.title: Changes in ownership and loss of control
formulas.idea: While control lasts, trades with NCI are equity moves; when control ends, everything is sold and what is kept is bought back at fair value.

master.name: Change without loss of control
master.expr: Equity adjustment = Consideration paid (or received) − Change in NCI carrying amount; NCI change = NCI × % transferred ÷ NCI %
master.logic: Buying more of your own house from a co-owner is not a profit; the difference sits in other equity.
master.cue: parent buys/sells shares but keeps control

items.name: Gain or loss on loss of control
items.expr: Gain = FV of consideration + FV of retained interest + NCI carrying amount − Net assets (incl. goodwill) derecognised ± OCI reclassified
items.logic: Sell the whole subsidiary on paper, keep the slice you still hold at today's value.
items.derive: When control is lost, the equity-transaction rule stops and P&L applies.
items.cue: parent sells down to an associate or investment; subsidiary issues shares to outsiders
items.trap: Carrying the retained stake at its old share of net assets instead of fair value.

formulas.title: Equity method
formulas.idea: The investment grows with the investor's share of profits and shrinks with dividends.

master.name: Carrying amount under the equity method
master.expr: Carrying amount = Cost + Share of post-acquisition profit (adjusted) + Share of OCI − Dividends received − Impairment
master.logic: Like a savings jar: add your share of what it earns, take out what it pays you.
master.cue: associate or joint venture; share of profit; dividend from associate

items.name: Goodwill or capital reserve on an associate
items.expr: Goodwill = Cost − Investor % × FV of net identifiable assets (inside the carrying amount)
items.logic: The premium paid stays inside the investment — not shown separately.
items.derive: Part of cost in the master formula.
items.cue: acquired 30% for ₹… when net assets were …
items.trap: Amortising or separately impairing goodwill in an associate.

items.name: Upstream/downstream unrealised profit
items.logic: Only the part of the profit you made 'with yourself' is unrealised; the unrelated investors' part is real.
items.derive: Adjusts the share of profit in the master formula.
items.hook: Associates: eliminate only your %. Subsidiaries: eliminate 100%.
items.cue: sales between investor and associate/JV with goods in stock

items.name: Losses beyond the investment
items.expr: Recognise losses until (equity-method carrying amount + long-term interests) = 0; then only legal/constructive obligations
items.logic: You cannot lose more than you put in, unless you promised to pay more.
items.cue: associate makes heavy losses; long-term loan to associate
items.trap: Ignoring long-term interests, or including trade receivables.

items.name: Gain on ceasing equity accounting
items.expr: Gain = FV of retained interest + Proceeds − Carrying amount + OCI reclassified
items.logic: Same idea as losing control of a subsidiary.
items.cue: associate stake sold down to a small investment
items.trap: Remeasuring when an associate becomes a joint venture (no remeasurement).

formulas.title: Other consolidation rules with numbers
formulas.idea: The same building blocks, applied to the special cases ICAI asks about.

master.name: Holding percentage for control and influence
master.expr: Voting % = Parent's direct holding + Holdings of its subsidiaries (not associates or joint ventures); include substantive potential voting rights
master.logic: Count every vote the group can actually direct.
master.cue: does P control or influence the investee?

items.name: Step acquisition: control obtained
items.expr: Goodwill = Consideration for new stake + FV of previously held interest + NCI − Net identifiable assets; Gain = FV of old stake − its carrying amount
items.logic: When control arrives the old stake is treated as sold and bought back.
items.derive: Feeds the consideration or net-asset terms of the goodwill formula.
items.example: See the linked SM illustrations and ICAI questions.

items.name: Significant influence presumption
items.expr: Significant influence presumed if group holds ≥ 20% of voting power (direct + through subsidiaries)
items.logic: Twenty per cent is a rebuttable rule of thumb.
items.derive: Feeds the consideration or net-asset terms of the goodwill formula.
items.example: See the linked SM illustrations and ICAI questions.

items.name: Control test
items.expr: Control = Power over relevant activities + Exposure to variable returns + Ability to use power to affect returns
items.derive: Feeds the consideration or net-asset terms of the goodwill formula.
items.example: See the linked SM illustrations and ICAI questions.

items.name: Investment entity
items.expr: Subsidiaries measured at FVTPL: Gain = Closing FV − Opening FV (no consolidation, except service subsidiaries)
items.logic: An investor that lives off fair-value gains reports fair values.
items.derive: Feeds the consideration or net-asset terms of the goodwill formula.
items.example: See the linked SM illustrations and ICAI questions.

items.name: Separate financial statements
items.expr: Investment at cost, as per Ind AS 109, or equity method (same for each category); dividend in P&L when the right is established
items.logic: The parent's own books show the investment, not the subsidiary's assets.
items.derive: Feeds the consideration or net-asset terms of the goodwill formula.
items.example: See the linked SM illustrations and ICAI questions.

items.name: Joint operation
items.expr: Joint operator recognises its own assets, liabilities, revenue and expenses + its share of joint ones; sale to the JO → profit only to the extent of the other parties' interests
items.logic: A joint operator owns slices of things directly, not a share in an entity.
items.derive: Feeds the consideration or net-asset terms of the goodwill formula.
items.cue: shared facility; rights to assets and obligations for liabilities
items.example: See the linked SM illustrations and ICAI questions.
